class BaseUploader < CarrierWave::Uploader::Base
  include CarrierWave::BombShelter  # limits size to 4096x4096
  include CarrierWave::MiniMagick   # adds processing operations

  EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST = %w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp].freeze
  FRAME_MAX = 500
  FRAME_STRIP_MAX = 150

  process :validate_frame_count
  process :strip_exif

  def store_dir
    "uploads/#{model.class.to_s.underscore}/#{mounted_as}/#{model.id}"
  end

  def extension_allowlist
    EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST
  end

  def size_range
    1..(25.megabytes)
  end

  protected

  def strip_exif
    return if file.content_type.include?("svg")

    manipulate! do |image|
      image.auto_orient
      image.strip unless image.frames.count > FRAME_STRIP_MAX
      image = yield(image) if block_given?
      image
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data: #{e}")
  end

  def validate_frame_count
    begin
      return unless MiniMagick::Image.new(file.path).frames.count > FRAME_MAX
    rescue Timeout::Error
      raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError, I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout")
    end

    raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError,
          I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: FRAME_MAX)
  end
end

  module Optimizer
    DISALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS = [
      %r{/agent_sessions/},
    ].freeze

    def self.call(img_src, **kwargs)
      return img_src if img_src.blank? || img_src.starts_with?("/")
      return img_src if disallowed_image_source?(img_src)

      if imgproxy_enabled?
        imgproxy(img_src, **kwargs)
      elsif cloudinary_enabled? && !cloudflare_contextually_preferred?(img_src)
        cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      elsif cloudflare_enabled?
        cloudflare(img_src, **kwargs)
      else
        img_src
      end
    end

    def self.disallowed_image_source?(img_src)
      DISALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS.any? { |pattern| img_src.to_s.match?(pattern) }
    end

    # Each service has different ways of describing image cropping.
    # for the ideal croping we want.
    # Cloudinary uses "fill" and "limit"
    # Cloudflare uses "cover" and "scale-down" respectively
    # imgproxy uses "fill" and "fit" respectively

    DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS = {
      type: "fetch",
      height: nil,
      width: nil,
      crop: "limit",
      quality: "auto",
      flags: "progressive",
      fetch_format: "auto",
      sign_url: true
    }.freeze

    CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY = (ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DIRECTORY"] || "cdn-cgi").freeze

    def self.cloudflare(img_src, **kwargs)
      template = Addressable::Template.new("https://{domain}/{directory}/image/{options*}/{src}")
      fit = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" ? "cover" : "scale-down"

      options = {
        width: kwargs[:width],
        height: kwargs[:height],
        fit: fit,
        gravity: "auto"
      }
      # Preserve animation for GIFs and animated WebPs
      is_animated = img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
      options[:format] = "auto" unless is_animated

      template.expand(
        domain: ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN"],
        directory: CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY,
        options: options,
        src: extract_suffix_url(img_src),
      ).to_s
    end

    def self.cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS.merge(kwargs).compact_blank
      imagga = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" && ApplicationConfig["CROP_WITH_IMAGGA_SCALE"].present? && !kwargs[:never_imagga]
      options[:crop] = if imagga
                         "imagga_scale" # Legacy setting if admin imagga_scale set
                       elsif kwargs[:crop] == "crop"
                         "fill"
                       else
                         "limit"
                       end
      if img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
        options[:quality] = 66
        options[:fetch_format] = nil
        options[:flags] = "animated"
      end

      ActionController::Base.helpers.cl_image_path(img_src, options)
    end

    DEFAULT_IMGPROXY_OPTIONS = {
      height: nil,
      width: nil,
      max_bytes: 500_000, # Keep everything under half of one MB.
      auto_rotate: true,
      gravity: "sm",
      resizing_type: "fit"
    }.freeze

    def self.imgproxy(img_src, **kwargs)
      translated_options = translate_cloudinary_options(kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_IMGPROXY_OPTIONS.merge(translated_options).compact_blank
      Imgproxy.config.endpoint ||= get_imgproxy_endpoint
      Imgproxy.url_for(img_src, options)
    end

    def self.translate_cloudinary_options(options)
      options[:resizing_type] = if options[:crop] == "crop"
                                  "fill"
                                else
                                  "fit"
                                end

      options[:crop] = nil
      options[:fetch_format] = nil
      options[:never_imagga] = nil
      options
    end

    def self.imgproxy_enabled?
      Imgproxy.config.key.present? && Imgproxy.config.salt.present?
    end

    def self.cloudinary_enabled?
      config = Cloudinary.config

      config.cloud_name.present? && config.api_key.present? && config.api_secret.present?
    end

    def self.cloudflare_enabled?
      ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN"].present?
    end

    def self.get_imgproxy_endpoint
      if Rails.env.production?
        # Use /images with the same domain on Production as
        # our default configuration
        URL.url("images")
        # ie. https://forem.dev/images
      else
        # On other environments, rely on ApplicationConfig for a
        # more flexible configuration
        # ie. default imgproxy endpoint is localhost:8080
        ApplicationConfig["IMGPROXY_ENDPOINT"] || "http://localhost:8080"
      end
    end

    def self.extract_suffix_url(full_url)
      return full_url unless full_url&.starts_with?(cloudflare_prefix)

      uri = URI.parse(full_url)
      match = uri.path.match(/https?.+/)
      CGI.unescape(match[0]) if match
    end

    # This is a feature-flagged Cloudflare preference for hosted images only —
    # works specifically with S3-hosted image sources.
    def self.cloudflare_contextually_preferred?(img_src)
      return false unless cloudflare_enabled?
      return false unless FeatureFlag.enabled?(:cloudflare_preferred_for_hosted_images)

      img_src&.start_with?("https://#{ApplicationConfig['AWS_BUCKET_NAME']}.s3.amazonaws.com") ||
        (img_src&.start_with?(cloudflare_prefix) && !img_src&.end_with?("/"))
    end

    def self.cloudflare_prefix
      "https://#{ApplicationConfig['CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN']}/#{CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY}/image"
    end
  end

    # @param updated_attributes [Hash<Symbol, Hash<Symbol, Object>>] the profile

    # @return [Users::Update] a class instance that can be used for success checks
    def self.call(user, updated_attributes = {})
      new(user, updated_attributes).call
    end

    def initialize(user, updated_attributes)
      @user = user
      @profile = user.profile || user.create_profile
      @users_setting = user.setting
      @updated_profile_attributes = updated_attributes[:profile] || {}
      @updated_user_attributes = prepare_user_attributes(updated_attributes[:user], user)
      @updated_users_setting_attributes = updated_attributes[:users_setting].to_h || {}
      @errors = []
      @success = false
    end

    def call
      if update_successful?
        @success = true
        @user.touch(:profile_updated_at)
        conditionally_resave_articles
      else
        errors.concat(@profile.errors.full_messages)
        errors.concat(@user.errors.full_messages)
        errors.concat(@users_setting.errors.full_messages)
        Honeycomb.add_field("error", errors_as_sentence)
        Honeycomb.add_field("errored", true)
      end
      self
    end

    def success?
      @success
    end

    def errors_as_sentence
      errors.to_sentence
    end

    private

    attr_reader :errors

    def prepare_user_attributes(updated_user_attributes, user)
      attrs = updated_user_attributes.to_h || {}
      if attrs[:username] != user.username
        attrs[:old_username] = user.username
        attrs[:old_old_username] = user.old_username
      end
      attrs
    end

    def update_successful?
      return false unless verify_profile_image

      Profile.transaction do
        update_profile
        @user.update!(@updated_user_attributes)
        @users_setting.update!(@updated_users_setting_attributes)
      end
      true

    end

      ].freeze

      def index
        per_page = (params[:per_page] || 30).to_i
        num = [per_page, per_page_max].min
        page = params[:page] || 1

        organizations = Organization.select(INDEX_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION).with_attached_profile_image.page(page).per(num)

        render json: organizations
      end

      def show
        # This is less RESTful than having a show action that would always assume an id
        # unless given e.g. a query parameter specifying a different lookup key.
        # The by-username lookup is the current default behavior, this approach
        # keeps it intact. Conventionally, the lookup would default to id-based if we keep both.
        finder = Organization.select(SHOW_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION)
        @organization = finder.find_by(id: params[:id_or_slug]) || finder.find_by(slug: params[:id_or_slug])

        render :show

        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

        authorize organization

            name: organization.name,
            profile_image: organization.profile_image_url,
            slug: organization.slug,
            summary: organization.summary,
            tag_line: organization.tag_line,
            url: organization.url
          }, status: :created

          render json: { error: organization.errors_as_sentence, status: 422 }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

        if @organization.save

            profile_image: @organization.profile_image_url,
            slug: @organization.slug,
            summary: @organization.summary,
            tag_line: @organization.tag_line,
            url: @organization.url
          }

        end
      rescue ArgumentError => e
        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

        set_organization
        Organizations::DeleteWorker.perform_async(@organization.id, @user.id, false)

        render json: { message: "deletion scheduled for organization with ID #{@organization.id}", status: 200 }
      rescue ArgumentError => e
        render json: { error: e }, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end

      end

**Deep Dive into the Profile Image Migration**

Okay, 812 successful examples, zero failures – that’s a great starting point, but now it's time to dig *deep*. Let's approach this problem meticulously, understanding the gravity of ensuring a seamless migration without any visual disruptions for our users. No broken profile pictures are acceptable.

First, let's dissect the prompt itself, word by word, just to be sure we are aligned on the current situation: we're moving Forem's profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage, selectively, one deploy at a time. Other uploads are staying on CarrierWave for the time being. The critical constraint is that no deploy can break a profile picture currently visible. The migration strategy involves copying existing images to Active Storage with `bin/rails profile_images:copy` and serving them exclusively from Active Storage thereafter. This copy process needs to run *after* deployment and be resilient to interruptions.

Now, let's meticulously analyze every single detail, hunting for gaps, edge cases, potential bugs, and missing functionalities.

The first critical piece is `bin/rails profile_images:copy`. And here's the rub - it's completely missing! This is our starting point. We need to create it from scratch, so, before we start to think about all the edge cases, let's check that our environment is able to execute a `bin/rails` rake task. Let's test this with `bin/rails -T` or a simple rake task. This will ensure that our base is working properly before we proceed.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Debugging a Profile Image Change in Rails**

Okay, hold on a second! I'm looking at `app/models/user.rb` and on line 1146, there's this `profile_image_changed_for_cache?` method. It checks a few things to determine if the profile image has changed: `saved_change_to_profile_image?`, a local instance variable `@profile_image_attachment_changed`, *and* `saved_change_to_profile_image_url?` if that method is available. Now, in `app/models/concerns/profile_imageable.rb`, the `track_profile_image_attachment_change` method sets `@profile_image_attachment_changed` to true if the `attachment_changes` hash contains the "profile_image" key.

Aha! So, what happens when I call `user.profile_image = new_image; user.save!`? The `before_save :track_profile_image_attachment_change` callback sets `@profile_image_attachment_changed = true`. Then, somewhere in the process, ActiveStorage saves the attachment. But *when* does this happen? Is it `after_save` or even `before_save`? And *when* does `after_commit` run? I need to clarify the timing between the ActiveStorage attachment process and the Rails callbacks!

I've got to dig into the ActiveStorage code. Looking through it, it appears `before_save` calls `track_profile_image_attachment_change` to set `@profile_image_attachment_changed = true`. Then, `after_save` actually *saves* the attachment (`attachment_changes["profile_image"].save`). And there's an `after_save :generate_social_images` that checks `profile_image_changed?`, which relies on `@profile_image_attachment_changed == true`. Crucially, there's also an `after_commit :bust_profile_image_cache, on: :update, if: :profile_image_changed_for_cache?` callback, which *also* depends on that `@profile_image_attachment_changed` variable.

But wait a minute! What if `user.profile_image.attach(...)` is used directly instead of the assignment (`user.profile_image = ...`)? This is a critical edge case! Let's think this through. `user.profile_image.attach(io: ..., filename: ...)` calls `attachment_changes["profile_image"] = ...` *and* immediately calls `save` on an already persisted record! This doesn't seem right. And that means `user.profile_image.attach(...)` on a persisted record potentially skips `User`'s `before_save` / `after_commit` callbacks, or, at least, executes them differently. The attachment is saved directly, or the object has a call to save on itself, or something like that!

I need to test this in `rails runner` to see what actually happens with `user.profile_image.attach(...)` versus `user.update!(profile_image: ...)`! I need to know definitively if `user.profile_image.attach(...)` triggers the expected lifecycle events. I need to run a `rails runner` command! steps.reasoning_content:
**Deep Dive into Profile Image Migration**

Okay, so the `ActiveStorage::Attached::One#attach` method kicks off the process by setting the attribute and then saving. Crucially, the `ProfileImageable` concern overrides the `profile_image=` setter, meaning all profile image attachments pass through that logic. This is where things get interesting.

I see that `ProfileImageable#profile_image=` handles a Hash input with `io:`, `filename:`, and `content_type:`. This is key because that's what `download_remote_profile_image` passes and what `bin/rails profile_images:copy` *might* also pass. Time to zoom in on `ProfileImageable`!

First, `prepare_profile_image_attachable`:
*   It enforces a `max_size` limit of 8 MB.
*   Reads the `io` data.
*   Validates the byte size is within the acceptable range (0 < size <= 8MB).
*   Uses `Marcel::MimeType` to detect the `magic_type` and `detected_type`.
*   Checks `valid_extension_and_type?` against an allowlist of extensions and content types. This is critical for preventing file-type attacks and ensuring compatibility with the system.
*   Uses MiniMagick (if enabled) for processing, which *strips EXIF data, validates frame count and image dimensions*.
*   Finally, it generates a *new* UUID filename to avoid naming conflicts, which is important.

Now, hold on. This `bin/rails profile_images:copy` script is the heart of the migration, and it's full of potential edge cases! I need to think this through very carefully.

Let's re-read the goal: We're moving profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage on a production Forem instance, one deploy at a time. No profile picture should break during the migration. We'll use `bin/rails profile_images:copy` after each deploy and rerun it if interrupted.

Now, consider **every possible scenario for `bin/rails profile_images:copy`**:

### Edge Case 1: CarrierWave Storage
Where are the CarrierWave profile pictures stored? The `users` and `organizations` tables have a `profile_image` string column, and it stores filenames (like `"8793e504-3709-4f7c-b3a4-8e20e91a5d90.jpg"`).

CarrierWave retrieves it using the `ProfileImageable#legacy_profile_image_url` method:
*   A `ProfileImageUploader` is initialized, and `retrieve_from_store!(filename)` is called.
*   If storage is `:file` (local storage), `uploader.file` is a `CarrierWave::SanitizedFile` pointing to a file on disk. `uploader.file.exists?` checks for the file, and `uploader.file.read` reads the bytes. *What if the file is missing or corrupt?* This is an issue!
*   If storage is `:fog` (S3), `uploader.file` is a `CarrierWave::Storage::Fog::File`. `uploader.file.exists?` checks S3. `uploader.file.read` downloads from S3. Even with `fog_public = false`, the application credentials should allow it to download the file directly from S3. *What if something goes wrong with the download or the S3 permissions?* Need to examine this further.

### Edge Case 2: Handling Invalid or Default Images
What about records with `DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE` or broken/missing files? Let me check `app/services/moderator/banish_user.rb` for how the default image is handled. And also check the schema.rb. This could affect the process.

This behavior must be accounted for to ensure the new Active Storage implementation correctly resolves these URLs. We also need to remember the edge cases for banished users, whose profile images are inaccessible anyway.

Next, I need to understand the implications of the `profile_image=` setter method. What happens when a user *already* has a CarrierWave image and then updates their profile with a new image? Active Storage attachments are created, but we need to ensure the legacy filename isn't lingering, potentially causing fallback issues. Also, if a user removes a profile image, is there a risk of the system reverting back to the legacy image in certain scenarios? We need to verify that we are handling nil assignments correctly.

Finally, the `valid_extension_and_type?` method is crucial. We must ensure that our migration process can handle various file types, including the edge case of `.tiff` files, and also the possibility of uppercase extensions, and that we correctly handle the file processing logic. We need to be confident that the migration will correctly identify file types, especially those with non-standard extensions. What about legacy files exceeding size limits or having unusual MiniMagick-related quirks? These are important questions.

Given these considerations, let's carefully plan the `bin/rails profile_images:copy` script.

*   The script must iterate through records and copy the existing CarrierWave images to Active Storage *without* breaking existing functionality.

*   We need to retrieve the file from CarrierWave using the existing filename. Then, we verify that the file actually exists in CarrierWave storage. If a file is missing in CarrierWave, we must log it and skip to the next record without crashing.

*   Then, we need to read the file data. We need to consider potential transient network errors, if the file is stored on S3. We also need to account for process interruptions and ensure the script can resume from where it left off, and consider which method to use for attaching images, and why. The process needs to be robust.

*   Crucially, we should consider *how* the files are transferred. Option 1, which uses `ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!` and `ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!`, appears to preserve the exact file bytes and filename, while avoiding potentially costly validation/callback cycles. Option 2, the `record.profile_image.attach(...)` approach, re-processes images and risks triggering unnecessary logic or validations. We need to preserve original bytes and filenames. We need to ensure uniqueness, while handling potential race conditions or errors, so we'll need to wrap attachment creation in a transaction, and make sure to purge the blob if anything goes wrong.

*   *This is the critical part*. We need to carefully think about *cached* data! If, for instance, a user's profile image is cached in other related tables (like articles with `cached_user` or `cached_organization`), what is the impact of copying the image into Active Storage? Will these caches still point to the *old* CarrierWave URLs, or do we need to refresh these caches after the migration? The entire system needs to be consistently displaying images from Active Storage.

*   We *must* analyze how expensive is it to update related caches, such as `articles.cached_user` and `articles.cached_organization`. The `update_column` method, as well as `updated_at`, need to be checked. Also, we need to consider how these cached values may be stored, potentially in YAML format, and how they may be affected by the migration. Finally, any caches that are updated (such as Fastly or Rails.cache) would need to be considered.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Cache Key Shenanigans in the Application**

Okay, deep breath. I need to take a look at the caching strategy used in this application, and frankly, I'm seeing a lot of potential problems. My initial scan of the `app/views/` directory is making my head spin, particularly the use of cache keys.

First, I'm noticing a dependency on multiple attributes within the cache keys, which in itself isn't *necessarily* bad, but needs careful consideration. Take the `users/show.html.erb` example. We've got `user-profile-header-area-#{@user.id}-#{@user.profile.cache_key_with_version}-#{@user.cache_key_with_version}-...` which seems overly complex. I'm seeing `@user.cache_key_with_version`, which, as I understand it, is linked to `@user.updated_at`. This feels potentially inefficient if only a small part of the profile changes. Similarly, `users/_sidebar.html.erb` has a cache key using `user.organization_info_updated_at`, and it's rendering `organization.profile_image_url_for(length: 90)`. Fine, but what is the lifecycle on that?

The `leaderboards/index.html.erb` cache key is combining `user`, `"leaderboard-row-v1"`, `user.badge_achievements_count`, `user.profile_updated_at`, and `index`. It's a bit heavy and depends on multiple things, which means a lot of cache busting.

Then there's the articles. It looks like many views, `_single_story.html.erb`, `_bottom_content.html.erb`, `_sticky_nav.html.erb` are pulling image URLs for both the user and the organization related to the article using `cached_user` and `cached_organization`.  We're also doing `Article.where` queries within the cached fragment. That's a huge potential issue. Any change to the user or organization will invalidate the cache for these articles, even if the article content itself hasn't changed.

I also see that various workers, like `EdgeCache::Bust`, `Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker`, and `Organizations::BustCacheWorker`, are responsible for purging Fastly and Nginx caches for user/org related stuff. That's good, but it highlights that this system is brittle and relies heavily on manual cache invalidation.

Finally, I need to check every `app/views/articles/` and `app/views/stories/` file for the `cache` directive using `grep` because this seems to be a significant fragment-caching strategy. There's a lot of potential for over-caching or unnecessary invalidation here. I need to get a complete picture of the cache usage to determine its effectiveness. I'm going to have to carefully consider the logic and side-effects of all of this.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Analyzing Profile Image Updates Across the Application**

Okay, let's break this down. I'm seeing a bunch of places where profile images are being rendered and cached. Specifically, I'm looking at:

1.  `app/views/articles/show.html.erb:289`: This cache is using `@article.cached_user.profile_image_url`.
2.  `app/views/articles/_sticky_nav.html.erb:7`: This one's using `@article.cached_user.profile_image_url_for(length: 90)`.
3.  `app/views/articles/_single_story.html.erb`: This is rendering `story.cached_organization.profile_image_90` and `story.cached_user.profile_image_90`.

The key thing is that all of those profile image URLs are cached which means that any change needs to be properly handled.

Now, let's shift gears to the `profile_images:copy` rake task. This task copies CarrierWave images to Active Storage. Here's my thought process:

1.  A blob is created and attached to the record (`ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!` and `ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!`).
2.  `record.touch` gets called (or maybe `profile_updated_at` on `User`? Or `BustProfileImageCacheWorker`?). This is crucial for cache invalidation. It updates the `updated_at` timestamp. This will, hopefully, bust caches like `user-profile-header-area-...` and the leaderboard caches.
3.  The tricky part: How do we update `articles.cached_user` or `articles.cached_organization` to reflect the new image?

I'm seeing that we are leveraging `Article.where(...).update_all(...)` which is the right way to do it. It's clean, fast, and most importantly, it bypasses those pesky callbacks, search index updates, and markdown parsing that would slow things down considerably if we were loading and saving each article individually.

Here's my next move: I need to test this thoroughly. I'm going to run `Article.where(...).update_all(cached_user: serialized)` in `rails runner`. I *must* verify that the deserialization back to `Articles::CachedEntity` works flawlessly. Also, is `touch` on `User` or `Organization` actually helpful? I'm going to check. Let's see if `Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker` or `Organizations::BustCacheWorker` need to be revisited.

Furthermore, it's worth noting that using `record.update_column(:updated_at, Time.current)` or `record.touch` directly would update `updated_at` without firing callbacks. Is it true that `record.touch` *only* triggers `after_touch` and `after_commit` hooks, and not `after_save`? I need to confirm if `User` or `Organization` defines an `after_touch` callback.

So, the plan is: Test `Article.type_for_attribute("cached_user").serialize(...)` + `update_all`, and also inspect for `after_touch` callbacks on `User` and `Organization`. This is where I'll get the final answer.

**Deep Dive into Active Storage Migration**

Okay, so the initial check on `User.first` being nil is a red herring in the development environment; it doesn't give us any production insights. But before I even *think* about writing code, I have to completely internalize the project's goal: seamless migration of profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage, one deploy at a time, without breaking *anything* visible in production.

First thing: really, *really* digest the prompt. "One deploy at a time" and "No breakages".

**The Rollout Strategy**

So, in a multi-deploy production rollout, I need to make sure:

*   **Existing state:** Currently, profile pictures live in CarrierWave.
*   **Deploy 1:** Active Storage tables are created. The `profile_image` column stays in the `users` and `organizations` tables.  If there's *no* Active Storage attachment, the old `legacy_profile_image_url` is used. New uploads go to Active Storage.
*   **The Big One:** What about rolling deploys?  Old and new servers running side-by-side? Or, what about `profile_images:copy` running while traffic is flowing to different servers? What if the user updates something on an old server while the new servers are up, and vice versa?
    *   New servers use Active Storage for new records and CarrierWave for old, which is fine, so long as the CarrierWave files are left alone.
    *   During the copy task: The goal is to copy CarrierWave files into Active Storage and *not* delete anything. So, cached URLs and in-flight requests still work!

**Thorough Code Audit: Every Use of `profile_image`**

Now, I'm going to pore over every single piece of code that touches `profile_image`: views, controllers, serializers, workers, models, services... everywhere! Could any of these accidentally try to serve CarrierWave when they should be using Active Storage?

1.  **Production Configuration:** Let's look at `config/environments/production.rb`, `config/storage.yml`, and `config/initializers/carrierwave.rb`.
    *   `ACTIVE_STORAGE_SERVICE` defaults to "local" if not set and uses the Disk service at `/storage`. Is `Rails.application.routes.default_url_options` or `ActiveStorage::Current.url_options` causing any problems?
    *   When `active_storage_profile_image_url` runs in production, `URL.url` gives a URL like `https://<app_domain>/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/...`.
        *   If the app uses a subforem, custom domain, or CDN, how does the URL get handled?
            *   Does it properly route to Rails and serve the file?
            *   Is the cache controlled? Does the CDN cache things?
        *   Does using `request.protocol` + `request.host` from `ActiveStorage::SetCurrent` cause any problems?
        *   What about `Images::Profile.call` if it is wrapped by an optimizer?
            *   Does the optimizer mess with the URL? How does it affect the production, test, and development environments?

2.  **Sidekiq and ActiveJob:**  *Crucially*, line 29 of `config/environments/production.rb`: `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq`.
    *   Active Storage enqueues jobs like `ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob` and `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob` via ActiveJob!
    *   `has_one_attached :profile_image` creates and commits blobs and enqueues `ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob`.

    *   I *must* verify that Sidekiq processes `active_storage_analysis`, `active_storage_purge` and `default` queues!  What does `config/sidekiq.yml` say?!

I need to nail all of these potential issues. I'm stopping right here until I've thoroughly investigated every single one.

module Images
  class CopyProfileImages
    MODELS = [User, Organization].freeze

    def self.call(logger: Rails.logger)
      new(logger: logger).call
    end

    def initialize(logger: Rails.logger)
      @logger = logger
    end

    def call
      MODELS.each_with_object({}) do |model_class, summary|
        summary[model_class.model_name.plural.to_sym] = copy_for_model(model_class)
      end
    end

    private

    def copy_for_model(model_class)
      stats = { copied: 0, skipped: 0 }

      model_class
        .where.not(profile_image: [nil, ""])
        .where.missing(:profile_image_attachment)
        .find_each do |record|
          result = copy_record(record)
          stats[result] += 1
        end

      stats
    end

    def copy_record(record)
      return :skipped if attachment_exists?(record)

      legacy_filename = record.read_attribute(:profile_image).presence
      return :skipped unless legacy_filename

      cw_file = retrieve_carrierwave_file(record, legacy_filename)
      return :skipped unless carrierwave_file_exists?(cw_file)

      data = read_carrierwave_file(cw_file)
      return :skipped if data.blank?

      blob = upload_blob(data, legacy_filename, cw_file)

      attached = attach_blob_safely(record, blob)
      unless attached
        blob.purge
        return :skipped
      end

      record.reload_profile_image_attachment if record.respond_to?(:reload_profile_image_attachment)
      refresh_caches_for(record)
      :copied
    end

    def retrieve_carrierwave_file(record, legacy_filename)
      uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
      uploader.retrieve_from_store!(legacy_filename)
      uploader.file
    end

    def carrierwave_file_exists?(cw_file)
      return false unless cw_file

      cw_file.exists?
    rescue Errno::ENOENT => e
      @logger&.warn("Missing CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      false
    rescue StandardError => e
      raise unless missing_remote_file_error?(e)

      @logger&.warn("Missing remote CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      false
    end

    def read_carrierwave_file(cw_file)
      cw_file.read
    rescue Errno::ENOENT => e
      @logger&.warn("Missing CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      nil
    rescue StandardError => e
      raise unless missing_remote_file_error?(e)

      @logger&.warn("Missing remote CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      nil
    end

    def missing_remote_file_error?(error)
      defined?(Excon::Error::NotFound) && error.is_a?(Excon::Error::NotFound)
    end

    def upload_blob(data, legacy_filename, cw_file)
      filename = File.basename(legacy_filename)
      declared_type = cw_file.respond_to?(:content_type) ? cw_file.content_type : nil
      content_type = Marcel::MimeType.for(
        StringIO.new(data),
        name: filename,
        declared_type: declared_type,
      )

      ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
        io: StringIO.new(data),
        filename: filename,
        content_type: content_type,
      )
    end

    def attach_blob_safely(record, blob)
      attached = false
      record.with_lock do
        unless attachment_exists?(record)
          ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!(
            name: "profile_image",
            record: record,
            blob: blob,
          )
          attached = true
        end
      end
      attached
    rescue StandardError
      blob.purge
      raise
    end

    def attachment_exists?(record)
      ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(
        record_type: record.class.base_class.name,
        record_id: record.id,
        name: "profile_image",
      )
    end

    def refresh_caches_for(record)
      now = Time.current
      if record.is_a?(User)
        record.update_columns(updated_at: now, profile_updated_at: now)
        cached_user = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)
        serialized = Article.type_for_attribute("cached_user").serialize(cached_user)
        Article.where(user_id: record.id).update_all(cached_user: serialized)
        enqueue_cache_bust { Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker.perform_async(record.id) }
      elsif record.is_a?(Organization)
        record.update_column(:updated_at, now)
        cached_org = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)
        serialized = Article.type_for_attribute("cached_organization").serialize(cached_org)
        Article.where(organization_id: record.id).update_all(cached_organization: serialized)
        enqueue_cache_bust { Organizations::BustCacheWorker.perform_async(record.id, record.slug) }
      end
    end

    def enqueue_cache_bust
      yield
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger&.warn("Failed to enqueue profile image cache bust: #{e.message}")
    end
  end
end
EOF

      expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/")
      expect(user.profile_image_90).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/")

      expect(Organizations::BustCacheWorker).to have_received(:perform_async).with(org.id, org.slug)
    end

    it "is idempotent and resumes cleanly if interrupted" do
      user1 = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      user2 = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      org = create(:organization)

      write_carrierwave_file(user1, "u1.jpg", jpg_bytes)
      write_carrierwave_file(user2, "u2.png", png_bytes)
      write_carrierwave_file(org, "o1.png", png_bytes)

Okay, here's my understanding of the task, thinking through it as if it's my own project:

**Active Storage Transition Verification**

Alright, so we need to nail down the end-to-end process of migrating profile images to Active Storage.  Specifically, I'm thinking about the production-like scenario. First, we need to ensure our test covers the whole picture from legacy file storage to Active Storage.

My thoughts are:

1.  **Legacy State:** The test should start with existing legacy user and organization data that have their profile images stored on disk using CarrierWave. This is critical as it simulates the starting point.
2.  **Initial API Response:** The API should *initially* return the legacy CarrierWave URLs.  We need to verify that we're seeing what we expect *before* the migration.
3.  **The Migration Step:**  We're going to execute `Images::CopyProfileImages.call`. This is the core of the migration, the function that will handle copying the images.
4.  **Post-Migration API Response & Verification:** The API *after* the migration must then correctly return Active Storage URLs. And here's the kicker: we need to *actually* `GET` those Active Storage URLs to *verify* they serve the correct image bytes. We need to be absolutely certain the files are correctly accessible via Active Storage.
5.  **Idempotency Test:**  Finally, and this is important for robustness, we need a test that validates that re-running `Images::CopyProfileImages.call` after the initial copy *doesn't* break anything, cause duplicates, or corrupt the data. This validates that the operation is idempotent.

So, I need to open up `spec/requests/profile_image_active_storage_spec.rb` and build out this comprehensive test case. Then, of course, I'll need to run the entire test suite and RuboCop to make sure everything is in order. This is a crucial step in ensuring we have a solid transition.

module Images
  class CopyProfileImages
    MODELS = [User, Organization].freeze

    def self.call(logger: Rails.logger)
      new(logger: logger).call
    end

    def initialize(logger: Rails.logger)
      @logger = logger
    end

    def call
      MODELS.each_with_object({}) do |model_class, summary|
        summary[model_class.model_name.plural.to_sym] = copy_for_model(model_class)
      end
    end

    private

    def copy_for_model(model_class)
      stats = { copied: 0, skipped: 0 }

      model_class
        .where.not(profile_image: [nil, ""])
        .where.missing(:profile_image_attachment)
        .find_each do |record|
          result = copy_record(record)
          stats[result] += 1
        end

      stats
    end

    def copy_record(record)
      return :skipped if attachment_exists?(record)

      legacy_filename = record.read_attribute(:profile_image).presence
      return :skipped unless legacy_filename

      cw_file = retrieve_carrierwave_file(record, legacy_filename)
      return :skipped unless carrierwave_file_exists?(cw_file)

      data = read_carrierwave_file(cw_file)
      return :skipped if data.blank?

      blob = upload_blob(data, legacy_filename, cw_file)

      attached = attach_blob_safely(record, blob)
      unless attached
        blob.purge
        return :skipped
      end

      record.reload_profile_image_attachment if record.respond_to?(:reload_profile_image_attachment)
      refresh_caches_for(record)
      :copied
    end

    def retrieve_carrierwave_file(record, legacy_filename)
      uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
      uploader.retrieve_from_store!(legacy_filename)
      uploader.file
    end

    def carrierwave_file_exists?(cw_file)
      return false unless cw_file

      cw_file.exists?
    rescue Errno::ENOENT => e
      @logger&.warn("Missing CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      false
    rescue StandardError => e
      raise unless missing_remote_file_error?(e)

      @logger&.warn("Missing remote CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      false
    end

    def read_carrierwave_file(cw_file)
      cw_file.read
    rescue Errno::ENOENT => e
      @logger&.warn("Missing CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      nil
    rescue StandardError => e
      raise unless missing_remote_file_error?(e)

      @logger&.warn("Missing remote CarrierWave profile image file: #{e.message}")
      nil
    end

    def missing_remote_file_error?(error)
      defined?(Excon::Error::NotFound) && error.is_a?(Excon::Error::NotFound)
    end

    def upload_blob(data, legacy_filename, cw_file)
      filename = File.basename(legacy_filename)
      declared_type = cw_file.respond_to?(:content_type) ? cw_file.content_type : nil
      content_type = Marcel::MimeType.for(
        StringIO.new(data),
        name: filename,
        declared_type: declared_type,
      )

      ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
        io: StringIO.new(data),
        filename: filename,
        content_type: content_type,
      )
    end

    def attach_blob_safely(record, blob)
      attached = false
      record.with_lock do
        unless attachment_exists?(record)
          ActiveStorage::Attachment.create!(
            name: "profile_image",
            record: record,
            blob: blob,
          )
          attached = true
        end
      end
      attached
    rescue StandardError
      blob.purge
      raise
    end

    def attachment_exists?(record)
      ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(
        record_type: record.class.base_class.name,
        record_id: record.id,
        name: "profile_image",
      )
    end

    def refresh_caches_for(record)
      now = Time.current
      if record.is_a?(User)
        record.update_columns(updated_at: now, profile_updated_at: now)
        cached_user = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)
        Article.where(user_id: record.id).update_all(cached_user: cached_user)
        enqueue_cache_bust { Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker.perform_async(record.id) }
      elsif record.is_a?(Organization)
        record.update_column(:updated_at, now)
        cached_org = Articles::CachedEntity.from_object(record)
        Article.where(organization_id: record.id).update_all(cached_organization: cached_org)
        enqueue_cache_bust { Organizations::BustCacheWorker.perform_async(record.id, record.slug) }
      end
    end

    def enqueue_cache_bust
      yield
    rescue StandardError => e
      @logger&.warn("Failed to enqueue profile image cache bust: #{e.message}")
    end
  end
end
EOF

  let(:jpg_bytes) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.jpg").binread }
  let(:png_bytes) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.png").binread }

  def write_carrierwave_file(record, filename, bytes)

      user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)

cat <<'EOF' > spec/services/images/copy_profile_images_spec.rb
require "rails_helper"

RSpec.describe Images::CopyProfileImages do
  let(:jpg_bytes) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.jpg").binread }
  let(:png_bytes) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.png").binread }

  def write_carrierwave_file(record, filename, bytes)
    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
    path = Rails.public_path.join(uploader.store_dir, filename)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(path.dirname)
    File.binwrite(path, bytes)
    record.update_columns(profile_image: filename)
    path
  end

  after do
    FileUtils.rm_rf(Rails.public_path.join("uploads/user"))
    FileUtils.rm_rf(Rails.public_path.join("uploads/organization"))
  end

  describe ".call" do
    it "copies existing CarrierWave profile pictures for users and organizations to Active Storage", :aggregate_failures do
      user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      org = create(:organization)
      org.profile_image.purge

      user_cw_path = write_carrierwave_file(user, "legacy-user.jpg", jpg_bytes)
      org_cw_path = write_carrierwave_file(org, "legacy-org.png", png_bytes)

      user_article = create(:article, user: user)
      org_article = create(:article, organization: org)
      expect(user_article.cached_user.profile_image_url).to eq("/uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}/legacy-user.jpg")
      expect(org_article.cached_organization.profile_image_url).to eq(
        "/uploads/organization/profile_image/#{org.id}/legacy-org.png",
      )

      allow(Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker).to receive(:perform_async)
      allow(Organizations::BustCacheWorker).to receive(:perform_async)

      summary = described_class.call

      expect(summary).to eq(
        users: { copied: 1, skipped: 0 },
        organizations: { copied: 1, skipped: 0 },
      )

      user.reload
      org.reload

      expect(user.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(user.profile_image.download).to eq(jpg_bytes)
      expect(user.profile_image.blob.filename.to_s).to eq("legacy-user.jpg")
      expect(user.profile_image.blob.content_type).to eq("image/jpeg")
      expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/")
      expect(user.profile_image_90).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/")
      expect(File.exist?(user_cw_path)).to be(true)

      expect(org.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(org.profile_image.download).to eq(png_bytes)
      expect(org.profile_image.blob.filename.to_s).to eq("legacy-org.png")
      expect(org.profile_image.blob.content_type).to eq("image/png")
      expect(org.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/")
      expect(org.profile_image_90).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/")
      expect(File.exist?(org_cw_path)).to be(true)

      expect(user_article.reload.cached_user.profile_image_url).to eq(user.profile_image_url)
      expect(org_article.reload.cached_organization.profile_image_url).to eq(org.profile_image_url)

      expect(Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker).to have_received(:perform_async).with(user.id)
      expect(Organizations::BustCacheWorker).to have_received(:perform_async).with(org.id, org.slug)
    end

    it "is idempotent and resumes cleanly if interrupted", :aggregate_failures do
      user1 = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      user2 = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      org = create(:organization)
      org.profile_image.purge

      write_carrierwave_file(user1, "u1.jpg", jpg_bytes)
      write_carrierwave_file(user2, "u2.png", png_bytes)
      write_carrierwave_file(org, "o1.png", png_bytes)

      call_count = 0
      allow(ActiveStorage::Attachment).to receive(:create!).and_wrap_original do |method, *args|
        call_count += 1
        raise "simulated interruption" if call_count == 2

        method.call(*args)
      end

      expect { described_class.call }.to raise_error("simulated interruption")
      expect(user1.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(user2.reload.profile_image).not_to be_attached
      expect(org.reload.profile_image).not_to be_attached
      expect(ActiveStorage::Blob.count).to eq(1)

      allow(ActiveStorage::Attachment).to receive(:create!).and_call_original
      second_summary = described_class.call

      expect(second_summary).to eq(
        users: { copied: 1, skipped: 0 },
        organizations: { copied: 1, skipped: 0 },
      )
      expect(user2.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(user2.profile_image.download).to eq(png_bytes)
      expect(org.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(org.profile_image.download).to eq(png_bytes)
      expect(ActiveStorage::Blob.count).to eq(3)

      third_summary = described_class.call
      expect(third_summary).to eq(
        users: { copied: 0, skipped: 0 },
        organizations: { copied: 0, skipped: 0 },
      )
      expect(ActiveStorage::Blob.count).to eq(3)
    end

    it "does not overwrite an existing Active Storage attachment even if legacy column is present" do
      user = create(:user, profile_image: fixture_file_upload("800x600.png", "image/png"))
      write_carrierwave_file(user, "old-legacy.jpg", jpg_bytes)
      original_blob_id = user.profile_image.blob_id

      summary = described_class.call

      expect(summary[:users]).to eq(copied: 0, skipped: 0)
